question:
(c) Na2O, Al2O3 and P4O10 are oxides of period 3. Explain using balanced equations, what is observed when each compound is reacted with:
(i) An alkali
(ii) An acid
(iii) Which oxide(s) in c(i) above will give a solution whose pH is higher than 7 in water?
modelAnswer:
(i) With alkali:
Na₂O: no reaction with NaOH (basic oxide).
Al₂O₃: Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO₂ + H₂O (dissolves).
P₄O₁₀: P₄O₁₀ + 12NaOH → 4Na₃PO₄ + 6H₂O (dissolves).

(ii) With acid:
Na₂O: Na₂O + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O (dissolves).
Al₂O₃: Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O (dissolves).
P₄O₁₀: no reaction with HCl (acidic oxide).

(iii) Only Na₂O gives pH > 7 in water (forms NaOH).
